sentences.en: Hello, hello hello, and welcome to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 大家好，欢迎收听 Leonardo English 的 English Learning for Curious Minds 节目。

sentences.en: The show where you can listen to fascinating stories, and learn weird and wonderful things about the world at the same time as improving your English.
sentences.zh: 在这个节目中，你可以听到迷人的故事，在提高英语水平的同时，了解世界上各种奇妙而有趣的事物。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, and today we are going to be talking about the UK General Election.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，今天我们要聊聊英国大选。

sentences.en: On May 22nd, Rishi Sunak surprised the nation by announcing that there will be a general election in the UK.
sentences.zh: 5月22日，Rishi Sunak 宣布英国将举行大选，这让全国感到意外。

sentences.en: It will take place on July the 4th, and by the end of the day the people of the United Kingdom may know that they will have a different Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 大选将于7月4日举行，到那天结束时，英国人民可能会迎来一位新的首相。

sentences.en: So, in this episode we are going to talk about why there is an election earlier than expected, what some of the key themes of the election may be, how the British political system works, what political pundits and polls are saying, and who the next British Prime Minister is likely to be.
sentences.zh: 所以，在本期节目中，我们将讨论为什么大选比预期提前了，大选的一些关键主题可能是什么，英国政治体系是如何运作的，政治评论员和民意调查怎么说，以及谁最有可能成为下一任英国首相。

sentences.en: OK then, let’s get right into it and talk about the next general election.
sentences.zh: 好了，让我们直接进入正题，聊聊接下来的大选。

sentences.en: There is a great British tradition of standing outside in the rain without an umbrella or a raincoat, and trying to pretend that everything is ok.
sentences.zh: 英国有一个伟大的传统，那就是站在雨中，既不打伞也不穿雨衣，还试图假装一切都很好。

sentences.en: And that was exactly what the British Prime Minister, Rishi Sunak, did on the afternoon of Wednesday the 22nd of May.
sentences.zh: 英国首相 Rishi Sunak 在5月22日星期三下午正是这么做的。

sentences.en: He stood outside 10 Downing Street, the home of the Prime Minister, and announced to a group of journalists that the next general election would be held in just over a month’s time.
sentences.zh: 他站在首相府唐宁街10号门外，向一群记者宣布，下一次大选将在一个多月后举行。

sentences.en: The rain poured down, his hair and jacket growing wetter by the minute.
sentences.zh: 大雨倾盆而下，他的头发和夹克每分钟都变得更湿。

sentences.en: Sunak didn’t mention the rain, he carried on as if everything was normal, in the great British tradition.
sentences.zh: Sunak 没有提到雨，他像往常一样继续，秉承了英国的优良传统。

sentences.en: But everything was not ok. The weather was not ok, that much was clear, but Sunak’s popularity, and that of his political party, the Conservatives, was at rock bottom.
sentences.zh: 但一切并不顺利。天气不好是显而易见的，但 Sunak 的支持率以及他所属的保守党（Conservatives）的支持率也处于谷底。

sentences.en: He was not a popular man, and it was surprising to onlookers that he had decided that then was the time to pull the trigger and call an earlier-than-expected election.
sentences.zh: 他并不是一个受欢迎的人，旁观者对他决定在那时“扣动扳机”宣布提前大选感到惊讶。

sentences.en: Now, let me give you a brief reminder about the state of British politics before we move on to the question of the election itself.
sentences.zh: 在在我们讨论选举本身之前，让我先简要提醒一下英国政治的现状。

sentences.en: The UK has been governed by the same political party, the Conservatives, since 2010, for 14 years.
sentences.zh: 自2010年以来，英国一直由同一个政党——保守党执政，至今已有14年。

sentences.en: During that time, the Conservatives have gone through 4 different leaders; David Cameron, Theresa May, Boris Johnson, and Liz Truss.
sentences.zh: 在此期间，保守党经历了四位不同的领导人：David Cameron、Theresa May、Boris Johnson 和 Liz Truss。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak is the fifth. His predecessor, Liz Truss, lasted for a mere 44 days, and Sunak has done slightly better, having led the country since October of 2022.
sentences.zh: Rishi Sunak 是第五位。他的前任 Liz Truss 仅在位44天，而 Sunak 的表现稍好一些，自2022年10月以来一直领导着这个国家。

sentences.en: If you are a seasoned listener to this show with an exceptional memory, you will remember that we ended episode number 327, on the ill-fated 44-days of Liz Truss, like this:
sentences.zh: 如果你是本节目的资深听众且记忆力超群，你会记得我们在第327期关于 Liz Truss 倒霉的44天任期的结尾是这样说的：

sentences.en: Sunak has until January of 2025 to call a general election, he has two years to rebuild trust and patch up the damage from the most chaotic period of recent British political history.
sentences.zh: Sunak 在2025年1月之前必须举行大选，他有两年的时间来重建信任，并弥补英国近代政治史上最混乱时期造成的损害。

sentences.en: It’s a monumental task that he has ahead of him, and all that remains to be said is let’s check in again in a couple of years and see whether he manages it.
sentences.zh: 他面临着一项艰巨的任务，剩下的只能说，让我们几年后再来看看他是否能成功。

sentences.en: It's kind of weird hearing your voice from a few years ago, but that was from an episode in December of 2022.
sentences.zh: 听到自己几年前的声音感觉有点奇怪，但那是2022年12月的一期节目。

sentences.en: Anyway, here we are, I’m recording this at the end of May in 2024, and we have an election coming up, a time for the British public to have its say on whether Rishi Sunak has managed to turn the ship around, and be able to secure victory for the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 无论如何，现在是2024年5月底，我正在录制这期节目，大选即将到来，这是英国公众对 Rishi Sunak 是否成功扭转局面并能为保守党赢得胜利发表意见的时候。

sentences.en: Almost all of the surveys, polls, and political pundits are in agreement about this: no.
sentences.zh: 几乎所有的调查、民意测验和政治评论员都达成了一致：没有。

sentences.en: Or rather, it seems incredibly unlikely that the Conservatives will win, and it would be the most monumental upset if they did manage to win.
sentences.zh: 或者更确切地说，保守党获胜的可能性微乎其微，如果他们真的赢了，那将是历史上最惊人的冷门。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak has seen his popularity drop further and further as time has passed.
sentences.zh: 随着时间的推移，Rishi Sunak 的支持率不断下滑。

sentences.en: There is nothing particularly unusual about that–it happens to most British Prime Ministers–but the extent of his unpopularity is unusual.
sentences.zh: 这并没有什么特别不寻常的——大多数英国首相都会经历这种情况——但他不受欢迎的程度却很不寻常。

sentences.en: In April of this year, one polling company revealed that its most recent poll made Sunak the least popular British Prime Minister in history, with only 16% of the population approving of the job that he was doing, and only 19% of the country saying that it was planning to vote for The Conservatives, Sunak’s political party.
sentences.zh: 今年4月，一家民调公司透露，其最新民调显示 Sunak 是历史上最不受欢迎的英国首相，只有16%的人对他所做的工作表示认可，只有19%的人表示计划投票给 Sunak 所属的保守党。

sentences.en: From his perceived weakness as a politician through to a mismanaged economy, there are numerous reasons that he has found himself more unpopular than any prime minister before.
sentences.zh: 从他被认为作为政治家的软弱，到经济管理不善，他发现自己比以往任何一位首相都更不受欢迎，原因有很多。

sentences.en: So, if he was and still is so unpopular, why did he call an election?
sentences.zh: 那么，既然他过去和现在都如此不受欢迎，他为什么要举行大选呢？

sentences.en: The last election was in December of 2019, so theoretically he had until January of 2025, another 6 months, to call another election, as the terms are for 5 years.
sentences.zh: 上次大选是在2019年12月，所以理论上他直到2025年1月（还有6个月）才需要举行下一次大选，因为任期是5年。

sentences.en: Most political commentators believed that he would call an election sometime in the autumn, after there was the chance for some more positive news about the economy, but he didn’t wait.
sentences.zh: 大多数政治评论员认为他会在秋季的某个时候举行大选，因为那时可能会有一些关于经济的更积极的消息，但他没有等。

sentences.en: So, why did he call an election now instead of in a few months time?
sentences.zh: 那么，为什么他现在就宣布大选，而不是几个月后呢？

sentences.en: According to political commentators, there are a few reasons.
sentences.zh: 根据政治评论员的说法，有几个原因。

sentences.en: Firstly, he recently announced lower inflation and lower migration numbers, and he can tell people that his government is now steering the country in the right direction.
sentences.zh: 首先，他最近宣布通胀率和移民人数有所下降，他可以告诉人们，他的政府现在正引导国家走向正确的方向。

sentences.en: Secondly, there might be progress before July in terms of sending asylum seekers to Rwanda, which will be popular with a particular set of British voters.
sentences.zh: 其次，在7月之前，将寻求庇护者送往卢旺达的计划可能会取得进展，这会受到特定英国选民群体的欢迎。

sentences.en: And if he waits until the end of the year and there still hasn’t been any progress on that front, it will underline his inability to get anything done.
sentences.zh: 如果他等到年底，而这方面仍然没有任何进展，那将突显他无力完成任何事情。

sentences.en: And thirdly there is the fact that he doesn’t want to be seen to have waited until the very last minute.
sentences.zh: 第三，事实是他不想被看作是等到了最后一刻。

sentences.en: As you may know, Rishi Sunak was not elected by the British public; he was elected by the members of the Conservative party after Liz Truss resigned.
sentences.zh: 你可能知道，Rishi Sunak 并不是由英国公众选出的；他是在 Liz Truss 辞职后由保守党成员选出的。

sentences.en: That’s just what happens when a Prime Minister resigns - there isn’t another general election, rather the new Prime Minister is the head of the governing party.
sentences.zh: 首相辞职时就是这样——不会举行另一次大选，而是由执政党的党首担任新首相。

sentences.en: So, according to one theory, he thinks that if he calls an election “early” he can more genuinely claim that he is giving the British public the chance to have its say about who it wants as its leader.
sentences.zh: 因此，根据一种理论，他认为如果他“提前”举行大选，他就可以更真诚地声称，他是在给英国公众机会，让他们对自己想要的领导人发表意见。

sentences.en: These theories could all be true, to a certain extent, if you believe that he believes that calling the election now is about increasing the probability of the Conservatives winning it.
sentences.zh: 如果你相信他认为现在举行大选是为了增加保守党获胜的可能性，那么这些理论在某种程度上可能都是正确的。

sentences.en: There is another category of theories which is that he has called the election this early so that he can lose the election with as little damage as possible, both to himself and the Conservative party.
sentences.zh: 还有另一类理论，即他这么早举行大选是为了尽可能减少对他个人和保守党的损害。

sentences.en: Firstly, there is the question of damage to Sunak himself.
sentences.zh: 首先是关于对 Sunak 本人的损害问题。

sentences.en: If he feels like he will lose the election by a lower margin in July than he would in December, well this helps his future career prospects, it helps him in his life after being Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 如果他觉得7月输掉选举的差距会比12月小，那么这有助于他未来的职业前景，有助于他卸任首相后的生活。

sentences.en: Now, he isn’t going to be strapped for cash, in need of money, as between himself and his wife he has a fortune of almost a billion Euros, but it is more a case of damage limitation, and allowing him to move on and get on with whatever his future plans might be without too much personal embarrassment.
sentences.zh: 现在，他并不会缺钱花，因为他和妻子拥有近10亿欧元的财富，但这更多是为了止损，让他能够继续前进，开展未来的计划，而不会感到太尴尬。

sentences.en: And talking about damage limitation to the Conservative party, there is also the theory that he has been pushed into calling an early election by members of his own political party.
sentences.zh: 谈到对保守党的止损，还有一种理论认为，他是被自己政党的成员逼迫提前举行大选的。

sentences.en: These are men and women who know that Sunak is very likely to lose the election, but believe that the longer he delays it, the fewer votes the Conservatives will receive, and the fewer MPs will be elected.
sentences.zh: 这些人知道 Sunak 很有可能输掉选举，但他们认为他拖得越久，保守党获得的选票就越少，当选的议员也就越少。

sentences.en: In both cases, whether he truly believes that he can win the election or whether he only wants to lose it as quickly and painlessly as possible, clearly he feels like this is more likely to happen in July rather than in December or January.
sentences.zh: 在这两种情况下，无论他是真的相信自己能赢，还是只想尽可能快、尽可能无痛地输掉选举，显然他觉得在7月比在12月或1月更有可能实现目标。

sentences.en: Now, this is probably a good point to talk about the practicalities of the UK electoral system, because it probably is different to the one in your country.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能是谈论英国选举制度实际运作的好时机，因为它可能与你所在国家的制度不同。

sentences.en: The UK operates a system called “first past the post”.
sentences.zh: 英国实行一种被称为“简单多数制”（first past the post）的制度。

sentences.en: How this works is that the country is divided into what are called constituencies, 650 in total.
sentences.zh: 它的运作方式是将全国划分为所谓的选区，总共650个。

sentences.en: Anyone can put themselves forward to be the elected official in a constituency.
sentences.zh: 任何人都可以挺身而出，竞选某个选区的民选官员。

sentences.en: You can be an independent candidate, but most candidates are aligned to a political party.
sentences.zh: 你可以作为独立候选人，但大多数候选人都隶属于某个政党。

sentences.en: Then, every eligible adult votes for the person they want in their constituency, in their geographical area.
sentences.zh: 然后，每个符合条件的成年人都会在他们所在的选区（即地理区域）投票给他们想要的人。

sentences.en: The person who gets the most votes becomes the elected official for that area, the member of parliament, or “MP” for short.
sentences.zh: 获得票数最多的人成为该地区的民选官员，即国会议员，简称“MP”。

sentences.en: The person who comes second gets nothing, so let’s say one candidate gets 50,000 votes and another candidate gets 50,001, the second candidate is elected and becomes an MP, and the first gets nothing, they go home empty handed.
sentences.zh: 第二名什么也得不到，所以假设一个候选人得到50,000票，另一个候选人得到50,001票，第二个候选人当选并成为议员，而第一个候选人则一无所获，空手而归。

sentences.en: All 650 areas do this, and then the winning candidates become MPs.
sentences.zh: 所有650个选区都这样做，然后获胜的候选人成为议员。

sentences.en: Now, almost all of these MPs are part of a political party, so the party with the most MPs forms a government.
sentences.zh: 现在，几乎所有这些议员都属于某个政党，因此拥有最多议员的政党将组建政府。

sentences.en: The most popular political party doesn’t always have a majority, it doesn't always have more than half of the MPs, so they have to form a coalition, but this first past the post system favours larger parties, so having coalition governments is less common than it is in countries with different voting systems, like Germany or Italy, for example.
sentences.zh: 最受欢迎的政党并不总是拥有多数席位，即并不总是拥有超过半数的议员，因此他们必须组建联合政府，但这种简单多数制有利于大党，因此组建联合政府的情况不如德国或意大利等采用不同投票制度的国家那么普遍。

sentences.en: To reiterate how this is different from a proportional voting system, in a proportional voting system, if a party gets, let’s say, 30% of the vote, they will have 30% of the representatives.
sentences.zh: 再次强调这与比例代表制有何不同：在比例代表制中，如果一个政党获得30%的选票，他们将拥有30%的代表席位。

sentences.en: In a first-past-the-post system, like in the United Kingdom, it is possible for a party that receives 30% of the vote to end up with 0% or even 100% of the representatives.
sentences.zh: 在像英国这样的简单多数制中，一个获得30%选票的政党最终可能获得0%甚至100%的代表席位。

sentences.en: Right, that’s the administrative bit out of the way, the bit about how the political system works.
sentences.zh: 好了，行政部分讲完了，也就是关于政治体系如何运作的部分。

sentences.en: Who are the other candidates then, who is going to be the next British Prime Minister if it isn’t Rishi.
sentences.zh: 那么其他候选人是谁呢？如果不是 Rishi，谁将成为下一任英国首相？

sentences.en: Well, there is really only one viable alternative.
sentences.zh: 嗯，其实只有一个可行的替代选择。

sentences.en: There are two dominant political parties in British politics: The Conservatives, which is traditionally right of centre, and Labour, which is traditionally left of centre.
sentences.zh: 英国政坛有两个主导政党：传统上属于中右翼的保守党和传统上属于中左翼的工党（Labour）。

sentences.en: You might have heard of the Liberal Democrats, the Scottish National Party, the Green party, or even UKIP.
sentences.zh: 你可能听说过自由民主党、苏格兰民族党、绿党，甚至英国独立党。

sentences.en: But these parties typically never get more than 20% of the MPs between them, so really it's a question of whether it will be a Labour or Conservative Party victory.
sentences.zh: 但这些政党加起来通常也拿不到超过20%的议席，所以这实际上是工党还是保守党获胜的问题。

sentences.en: And the leader of the Labour Party, the leader of the opposition, is a man called Keir Starmer.
sentences.zh: 工党领袖、反对党领袖是一个叫 Keir Starmer 的人。

sentences.en: He has been the leader since 2020, and his strategy ever since he was elected can probably be best described as “sit in the sidelines and let the Conservatives make the mistakes”.
sentences.zh: 他自2020年以来一直担任领袖，自当选以来，他的策略大概可以被描述为“坐山观虎斗，让保守党犯错”。

sentences.en: Throughout his time as the leader of the opposition he has been relatively coy, quite quiet, about what his policies would be were he Prime Minister.
sentences.zh: 在担任反对党领袖期间，对于如果他当上首相会采取什么政策，他一直比较含蓄，相当低调。

sentences.en: Instead, he has been very good at pointing out the mistakes of the Conservative government, and holding them to account.
sentences.zh: 相反，他非常擅长指出保守党政府的错误，并追究他们的责任。

sentences.en: His critics say that he hasn’t offered solutions, and it isn’t really clear what he stands for, but he has played a very canny political game by being relatively quiet and letting his opponents make the mistakes.
sentences.zh: 批评者说他没有提供解决方案，也不清楚他的立场是什么，但他玩了一场非常精明的政治游戏，通过保持相对低调，让对手犯错。

sentences.en: And he hasn’t had to wait long. Since only 2020, when he took over from Jeremy Corbyn, the Conservatives have had three leaders, they have grossly mishandled the pandemic, there has been serious economic mismanagement, and there have been numerous public embarrassments.
sentences.zh: 他也没等多久。自2020年他接替 Jeremy Corbyn 以来，保守党已经换了三位领导人，他们在疫情处理上表现极差，经济管理严重失当，还多次在公众面前丢脸。

sentences.en: And on a deeper and more important level, since the Conservatives first took office in 2010, the UK has not grown and prospered economically in a way that every single Conservative Prime Minister has said it would.
sentences.zh: 从更深层次、更重要的层面来看，自保守党于2010年首次执政以来，英国的经济增长和繁荣并没有达到每一位保守党首相所承诺的那样。

sentences.en: According to one report from last year, the average worker in the UK is £11,000 a year worse off than they were before the Conservatives, so that’s almost €15,000 a year worse off.
sentences.zh: 根据去年的一份报告，英国工人的平均年收入比保守党执政前减少了11,000英镑，也就是减少了近15,000欧元。

sentences.en: Wages have increased in nominal terms, but these increases have been eaten away by inflation, meaning that the average British worker hasn't had a real pay rise since the Conservatives took power.
sentences.zh: 名义工资虽然增加了，但这些增幅已被通货膨胀抵消，这意味着自保守党执政以来，英国工人的平均实际工资并没有增长。

sentences.en: Of course, inflation is a subject that has affected countries all over the world, and the Conservatives repeatedly remind people of this, pointing out that the Russian invasion of Ukraine and the COVID pandemic were the chief causes.
sentences.zh: 当然，通货膨胀是一个影响全球各国的问题，保守党也反复提醒人们这一点，指出俄罗斯入侵乌克兰和新冠疫情是主要原因。

sentences.en: But a stumbling economy and low wage growth were both things that Brits felt before either of these.
sentences.zh: 但在这些事件发生之前，英国人就已经感受到了经济蹒跚和工资增长缓慢。

sentences.en: This, combined with increasing waiting times at the NHS–the national healthcare system–increasing cuts to social services, and the sad reality that 4 million British children live in poverty, this is all ammunition that Keir Starmer has and undoubtedly will continue to use in his campaign.
sentences.zh: 加上 NHS（国家医疗服务体系）等待时间的增加、社会服务削减的加剧，以及400万英国儿童生活在贫困中的悲惨现实，这些都是 Keir Starmer 掌握的“弹药”，毫无疑问，他将在竞选中继续使用。

sentences.en: The country has had enough, it is time for “change”.
sentences.zh: 这个国家已经受够了，是时候做出“改变”了。

sentences.en: And indeed, when Keir Starmer gave his first speech after the announcement of the election, he stood in front of a podium with one word plastered in big capital letters: Change.
sentences.zh: 事实上，当 Keir Starmer 在宣布大选后发表第一次演讲时，他站在一个印有大写字母“CHANGE”（改变）的讲台前。

sentences.en: Rishi Sunak and the Conservatives continue to tell us that things are getting better, that you just need to trust us to turn the economy around, but they have been saying this for 14 years.
sentences.zh: Rishi Sunak 和保守党继续告诉我们情况正在好转，你们只需要相信我们能扭转经济，但他们已经说了14年了。

sentences.en: Enough is enough, so the theory goes. People are ready for a change, and although Keir Starmer might not have the X factor in terms of charisma or making grand speeches, the British people have had enough of the Conservatives.
sentences.zh: 理论上讲，受够了就是受够了。人们已经准备好迎接改变，虽然 Keir Starmer 在个人魅力或发表宏大演讲方面可能缺乏某种特质，但英国人民已经受够了保守党。

sentences.en: That is certainly what Keir Starmer is hoping for at least.
sentences.zh: 至少这肯定是 Keir Starmer 所希望的。

sentences.en: The Conservatives’ key message in the campaign will be about trust, that Labour cannot be trusted with the keys to the British economy, that Labour has no plan.
sentences.zh: 保守党在竞选中的关键信息将是关于信任，即不能把英国经济的钥匙交给工党，因为工党没有计划。

sentences.en: A phrase that Rishi Sunak has already been repeating again and again is “going back to square one”, meaning going back right to the start.
sentences.zh: Rishi Sunak 已经反复提及的一个词是“回到原点”（going back to square one），意思就是回到最开始的状态。

sentences.en: Rishi and the Conservatives have a plan, he says, it is starting to work, as people can see by inflation coming down and the situation starting to look slightly less grim.
sentences.zh: 他说，Rishi 和保守党有一个计划，而且这个计划正开始奏效，人们可以看到通胀正在下降，情况开始显得不那么严峻了。

sentences.en: A vote for Labour is a vote to rip up the Conservatives’ plan, to return to square one, and what’s more, square one without a plan about how to move forward.
sentences.zh: 投票给工党就是投票撕毁保守党的计划，回到原点，而且更糟糕的是，回到一个没有前进计划的原点。

sentences.en: Now, I told you at the start of the episode that Rishi Sunak made the announcement of the general election standing in the pouring rain, and it was all a bit embarrassing.
sentences.zh: 好了，我在节目开始时告诉过你们，Rishi Sunak 是在倾盆大雨中宣布大选的，这有点尴尬。

sentences.en: That wasn’t the only embarrassment. A group of mischievous Labour supporters had found out about the announcement beforehand, and had congregated outside the gates to Downing Street.
sentences.zh: 这还不是唯一的尴尬。一群调皮的工党支持者事先得知了这一消息，并聚集在唐宁街的大门外。

sentences.en: They brought a loudspeaker with them, and were playing the song “Things can only get better”, which was used by the Labour leader Tony Blair when he won the election in 1997.
sentences.zh: 他们带了一个扩音器，播放着歌曲《Things can only get better》，这首歌曾被工党领袖 Tony Blair 在1997年赢得大选时使用。

sentences.en: To his credit, Rishi Sunak managed to not be too put off, but he was almost drowned out by the noise of the song, you could barely hear him over the noise.
sentences.zh: 值得称赞的是，Rishi Sunak 设法没有受到太大干扰，但他几乎被歌声淹没了，在噪音中你几乎听不到他的声音。

sentences.en: It was not an auspicious start to the campaign, but the song was a fitting message.
sentences.zh: 这不是一个吉利的竞选开端，但这首歌传达的信息却很贴切。

sentences.en: Things can only get better. One imagines that Rishi might have thought that it’s not as if they could get much worse.
sentences.zh: 事情只会变得更好。人们想象 Rishi 可能会想，情况总不至于变得更糟了。

sentences.en: OK then, that is it for today's episode on the UK general election.
sentences.zh: 好了，今天关于英国大选的节目就到这里。

sentences.en: I hope it's been an interesting one, and that this has given you some background on how things might develop over the next few weeks.
sentences.zh: 我希望这期节目很有趣，并且能让你对未来几周局势的发展有一些背景了解。

sentences.en: You've been listening to English Learning for Curious Minds, by Leonardo English.
sentences.zh: 你收听的是 Leonardo English 的 English Learning for Curious Minds 节目。

sentences.en: I'm Alastair Budge, you stay safe, and I'll catch you in the next episode.
sentences.zh: 我是 Alastair Budge，祝大家平安，我们下期节目再见。
